dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 9949 IH: Safe Baby Formula Act of 2026
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Barrett introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce

form.official-title: To require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to conduct a study on the impacts of arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead in infant formula on infant health and establish standards for regulating the content of such substances in infant formula.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Safe Baby Formula Act of 2026.

Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall complete a study on the impacts of arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead in infant formula on infant health.

section.header: Prohibition of toxic metals in infant formula

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall establish evidence-based action levels with respect to arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead in infant formula.
In establishing an action level under subsection (a), the Secretary shall consider—

paragraph.text: the feasibility of complying with such action level;
the capacity of the Department of Health and Human Services to enforce such action level for food imported, or offered for import, into the United States; and
the impact of such action level on domestic food security.

section.text: In this Act, the term infant formula has the meaning given such term in section 201(z) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 321(z)).
